sections.title: Photography I
sections.description:
This introductory course will introduce students to the fundamental concepts, processes, and techniques of photography. We will explore the relationship between contemporary artists, the camera, and both the analog and digital realms, while also addressing key ethical and philosophical questions.
Throughout the semester, students will gain a solid understanding of photography’s technological and historical development through key images and genres, and its impact on contemporary culture. The focus will be on the working tools for personal expression and learning how to connect the visual, theoretical, and conceptual aspects of photography.
Technical instruction will cover 35mm SLR and DSLR camera operations, basic analogue darkroom processes, flatbed scanning, postproduction, basic lighting, Adobe Bridge, Camera Raw, and Photoshop. Readings, course materials, and discussions will critically examine the impact of imaging technologies on traditional practices, society, and art. Individual projects will explore themes such as the street, documentary, social issues, narrative, staging, identity, and augmented reality.
